spots.w: The island's main skatepark, by the sea next to the Monte cable car. Concrete, about 900 m², lit, free. Quarters, banks, funboxes, pyramid, rails, curbs. Busy after school, quiet in the morning.

A real inline speed-skating track (€619k, national championships June 2026), up in Prazeres on the dry south-west. Run by the club CDR Prazeres: ask the club before you skate. Their skaters also know where to get frames and wheels on the island.

spots.n: Skate Park Água de Pena (under the runway)
spots.w: Under the airport runway pillars, so it stays dry: the best rain option. Inside a paid sports complex (weekdays 10–18, shorter at weekends). The complex is run down and works were announced for 2026, so check recent photos.
Concrete skatepark in Machico, lit. Only known from the map data, no reviews found. Combine with the smooth seafront on the east side of the bay.
Roller skating track on the north side, probably the venue of the Biosfera Roller Skate race. Wetter side of the island. Access not checked.
Concrete pump track in the new sports park (opened July 2025), for skates, boards, bikes and scooters. The best confirmed new spot on the island.
Only known from the map data, tagged as a BMX track. Surface unknown: could be dirt. Check the satellite view before you drive there.

spots.n: Funchal: Praça do Povo and the marina
spots.w: The smooth part of Funchal's seafront: excellent concrete squares by Praça do Povo and along the marina, lit at night. Laps rather than a cruise. The rest of the seafront and Avenida Arriaga is Madeiran cobble: avoid. Cruise passengers fill it from about 10 to 17, so skate before 9 or after 18.

spots.n: Machico: east side of the bay
spots.w: Excellent concrete square and a 250 m asphalt path by the beach on the São Roque side of Machico bay. Flat and quiet. The town seafront is cobble. Jardins da Graça skatepark is a few minutes away.
Best bet for inline wheels and bearings (Oxelo wheels and bearings, Powerslide bearings). Frames are rare in store: call first. Can also order Decathlon's own items to the store.
The island's only real skate shop. Skateboard bearings are the same size (608) as inline bearings. Inline wheels and frames unlikely, but the staff know the local skaters.
Small pickup store: order on decathlon.pt and collect here. Little skate stock in the shop itself. Marketplace items (most frames) cannot be collected here and take 8–10 working days to Madeira.
Skate shop in the mall, mostly clothing. Maybe skateboard bearings (608 fits inlines). Inline wheels and frames unlikely. Sport Zone is in the same mall.

i.Address: Madeira Shopping, Caminho Santa Quitéria 45, Funchal

spots.w: May have complete recreational skates. Spare parts unlikely.

i.Address: Caminho de Santa Quitéria, Madeira Shopping, Funchal

spots.w: May have complete recreational skates. Spare parts unlikely.
Industrial bearings (NTN, Koyo, SNR), so standard 608 bearings, not skate-rated. Mainly sells to businesses: ask if they sell to the public.

i.Address: Rua do Ribeiro das Freiras 3, Caniço

spots.n: Ribeira Brava: old coast road cycleway
spots.w: Flat red-asphalt cycle lane, separated by a curb from a quiet road, along the old coast road west of Ribeira Brava: cliffs on one side, sea on the other, on the dry, sunny south-west. The last 340 m by town is excellent concrete. A dead end in the west (the old road beyond is closed by rockfall), so skate it out and back.

i.Traffic: own lane next to a quiet road
i.Street View: 2026: wide, smooth red asphalt the whole way

spots.w: Wide, flat concrete promenade along Calheta's sandy beach and marina on the driest, sunniest coast. Short, so do laps. Closed for a few weeks in January 2026 after rockfall, open again since.

i.Crowds: busy around the beach in the afternoon
i.Street View: smooth asphalt by the sea, concrete and pavers at the marina (2016–2024 photos)

spots.n: Funchal: Doca do Cavacas → Praia Formosa
spots.w: Concrete cycleway and promenade from the Doca do Cavacas tunnel to Praia Formosa beach. Sea views, some short ramps. The promenade further west to Câmara de Lobos is closed after Storm Charles (Nov 2026): check the barriers, crossing them gets fined.

i.Street View: wide smooth concrete, a few cracks by Praia Formosa

spots.n: CLOSED: Praia Formosa → Câmara de Lobos promenade
spots.w: The best concrete promenade on the island (2.6 km, along the cliffs to the pump track in Câmara de Lobos), but closed since Storm Charles on 10–11 Nov 2026: the sea broke part of the walkway. Still closed on 17 Nov for a technical check; about two weeks were estimated. Do not cross the barriers.

i.Street View: smooth concrete with drain covers (before the storm)

spots.w: Seafront promenade from the Lido pools, mostly paving stones in good condition, so expect joints. Funchal's seafront fills with cruise passengers from about 10 to 17: skate before 9 or after 18.

i.Street View: interlocking pavers with joints, a cobble stripe in places

spots.w: Wide seafront promenade in the small village of Jardim do Mar under steep cliffs, on the dry south-west. Looks even in Street View (the map data says paving stones). Nature and surf spot; quiet.

i.Street View: wide, even surface along the sea wall

spots.n: Funchal: Estrada Monumental cycle path (Lido → Praia Formosa)
spots.w: Concrete cycle path along Funchal's hotel road, linking the Lido to Praia Formosa above the closed seafront. Separated from the road by hedges and bollards, smooth red surface at the Lido end. City setting with traffic noise.

i.Traffic: own path next to a busy road
i.Street View: smooth red lane at the Lido end; elsewhere only seen from the road

spots.w: Short seafront promenade of large concrete plates in the banana village of Madalena do Mar, cliffs behind, waves alongside. Joints between the plates. South-west, dry side.
Paver promenade along the cliffs by the whale museum in Caniçal, on the far east. Narrow and with joints, but quiet and wild.

The longest smooth car-free route in the archipelago: 3.8 km of asphalt cycleway along the 9 km beach, gentle slopes, and the driest island. Rollerblading is explicitly allowed on the promenade. Needs the ferry from Funchal (about 2.5 h).

i.Street View: only from the road; the cycleway itself is not shown. The town promenade is cobble

spots.n: Car road: Madalena do Mar seafront (ER101)
spots.w: The old coast road through the banana village of Madalena do Mar, right along the sea. Wide and smooth asphalt, flat, and it looked quiet in Street View. A paver pavement runs next to it if cars come. Dry, sunny south-west; combine with the promenade at the west end.
spots.warn: Car road: you share it with traffic. In Portugal skaters count as pedestrians, so keep to the edge, skate in daylight and good visibility, and wear something bright.

i.Street View: 2026: wide smooth asphalt, few cars, sea wall on one side

spots.n: Car road: São Vicente coast road (ER101)
spots.w: Flat coast road at São Vicente on the north coast, between green cliffs and the sea. Smooth asphalt and little traffic in Street View. The north side is wetter: pick a dry day.
spots.warn: Car road: you share it with traffic. In Portugal skaters count as pedestrians, so keep to the edge, skate in daylight and good visibility, and wear something bright.

spots.n: Car road: Paul da Serra plateau (ER105/ER209)
spots.w: Asphalt road across the high plateau, a mostly gentle descent westwards from about 1,490 to 1,385 m (3–4 % on average): moorland, wind turbines, views and wide open nature. Often in fog and wind: go on a clear day. Drive up: every road down is long and steep with hairpins.
spots.warn: Car road: you share it with traffic. In Portugal skaters count as pedestrians, so keep to the edge, skate in daylight and good visibility, and wear something bright.

spots.n: Car road: Paul da Serra east, wind farm (ER105)
spots.w: The eastern end of the plateau road among the wind turbines and yellow broom at about 1,550 m. Smooth asphalt, wide open views. Same fog and wind warning as the rest of the plateau.
spots.warn: Car road: you share it with traffic. In Portugal skaters count as pedestrians, so keep to the edge, skate in daylight and good visibility, and wear something bright.

spots.w: Straight plateau road through heath and old laurel trees on the way to the Fanal forest. Good asphalt, but often deep in fog: only on a clear day.
spots.warn: Car road: you share it with traffic. In Portugal skaters count as pedestrians, so keep to the edge, skate in daylight and good visibility, and wear something bright.

spots.n: Car road: ER105 north plateau (towards Porto Moniz)
spots.w: Flat stretch of the plateau road north of Fanal, through heath and woodland at about 1,000 m. Smooth asphalt with centre lines.
spots.warn: Car road: you share it with traffic. In Portugal skaters count as pedestrians, so keep to the edge, skate in daylight and good visibility, and wear something bright.

spots.n: Car road: Caminho Lombo da Rocha, Prazeres
spots.w: Quiet village road on the Prazeres plateau with smooth asphalt and a pavement, close to the speed-skating track. Good for a warm-up or a few laps after the track.
spots.warn: Car road: you share it with traffic. In Portugal skaters count as pedestrians, so keep to the edge, skate in daylight and good visibility, and wear something bright.
